title: Creative Divergent Thinking
shortDescription: Alternative-uses and idea-fluency tasks that measure how many genuinely different directions you can generate.
longDescription: Creative Divergent Thinking combines two classic, complementary creativity paradigms. The Alternative Uses Task (Guilford, 1967) asks you to generate as many different uses as you can for an everyday object — the foundational measure of idea fluency and divergent thinking, scored here by AI interpretation rather than a right/wrong answer, since the point is open-ended generation. The Remote Associates Test (Mednick, 1962) asks you to find the single word that connects three seemingly unrelated words — a convergent-creativity measure with objectively correct answers, scored deterministically.
sourceNote: The 5 Remote Associates Test items are original word triads written to implement Mednick's compound-word-association format, hand-verified for validity (each connecting word forms a real compound/phrase with all three given words) rather than reused from Mednick's original item bank, which this platform can't verify reproducing correctly from memory. The 5 Alternative Uses Task prompts follow Guilford's original open-ended format directly — there's no fixed answer key to reproduce, so no adaptation was needed there. Following the same policy as Creative Assessment: the open_creative items never feed the deterministic score; they're passed to the AI interpretation layer only (src/lib/ai/interpretation.ts), same policy documented there.

sections.name: Remote Associates
sections.description: Find the single word that connects three given words.
sections.instructions: Each item gives three words. Choose the word that forms a real compound word or common phrase with all three.

sections.name: Alternative Uses
sections.description: Generate as many different uses as you can for an everyday object.
sections.instructions: List as many different, genuinely distinct uses as you can think of. Quantity and variety both matter more than any single "best" answer.

scoringDimensions.label: Remote Associates (Convergent Creativity)
scoringDimensions.description: Finding the single connecting concept across three unrelated words.

resultRanges.title: Developing
resultRanges.description: Spotting the connecting concept across unrelated words is difficult right now — your idea-generation on the alternative-uses prompts is interpreted separately below.
recommendations: Practice free-associating around each given word before looking for overlap with the others
For alternative uses, push past the first 2-3 obvious answers — genuinely different categories of use are what's being measured
Read your AI interpretation below for feedback on the open-ended prompts specifically

resultRanges.title: Average
resultRanges.description: Some remote-associate connections found, others elusive — a normal split on a genuinely difficult task type.
recommendations: Try approaching each word from multiple senses (literal, compound, homophone) before moving on
On alternative uses, deliberately shift categories (not just size/shape variations of the same idea)

resultRanges.title: Strong
resultRanges.description: Reliable at finding the connecting concept across most word triads.
recommendations: Push into remote associates with less obvious connecting words to sharpen this further
Notice which alternative-uses categories you gravitate toward, and deliberately branch into unfamiliar ones

resultRanges.title: Very Strong
resultRanges.description: Consistently finds the connecting concept, including on the less obvious triads.
recommendations: This convergent-creativity skill pairs well with strong divergent output — check your AI interpretation for how they compare
Try timed remote-associates practice to push speed alongside accuracy

resultRanges.title: Exceptional
resultRanges.description: Near-perfect at finding the connecting concept across every word triad.
recommendations: This level of associative fluency is a genuine asset in ideation-heavy or naming-heavy work
Consider how it pairs with your divergent-thinking results from the alternative-uses prompts
